solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Secretary left State conference (7)

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: A secretary quits a state-level conference.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' sits capitalised as though it were a government body; it is the verb 'to state'. A palaver was originally a parley between traders and local people.
annotation.definitionFit: A palaver is a long talk or conference, now usually a tedious one.

entries.clue: Charming party bar served up beer bottles (8)

indicatorNotes.served up: in a down entry, served upward reads the word from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.bottles: the beer holds the other letters inside it as a bottle holds a drink

blocks.note: ale is beer; it bottles, or holds, the party and the reversed bar

annotation.surface: A charming party where the bar serves bottled beer.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'bar' a pub counter and 'served up' something a barman does; together they are an instruction to write BAR upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Adorable and charming both describe someone delightful to be with.

entries.clue: Most furious, Regina rudely discharged servant (8)

indicatorNotes.rudely: treating REGINA roughly scrambles her letters
indicatorNotes.discharged: a servant with the contents discharged keeps only the shell S…T

annotation.surface: Queen Regina, at her angriest, sacks a servant with rude words.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Discharged' reads as sacked; here it means emptied, the servant losing everything between S and T.
annotation.definitionFit: Angriest is the superlative of angry, so it means most furious.

entries.clue: Shock from rubbing plates? (10)

blocks.note: read as a jolt of static electricity, and meant as a violent tremor of the ground
read as polishing the crockery, and meant as the tectonic plates of the earth's crust grinding past each other

annotation.surface: Someone gets a static shock from polishing the crockery.
annotation.walkthrough: The plates sound like dinner plates, and a shock from rubbing them sounds like static electricity. The plates are tectonic, grinding past each other.
annotation.definitionFit: An earthquake is a shock caused when tectonic plates slip against each other.

entries.clue: Turn up gas ring, that’ll help to set the pudding (4)

annotation.definition: that’ll help to set the pudding

indicatorNotes.Turn up: in a down entry, turning a word up writes it from the bottom

blocks.note: O is round like a ring

annotation.surface: A cook turns up the gas ring so the pudding will set.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turn up gas ring' is a perfectly sensible kitchen instruction; it is really GAS reversed plus a ring-shaped letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Sago is a starch that swells and thickens a milk pudding as it cooks.

entries.clue: Smile when receiving Liberal Democrat old woman (6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: the smile takes the party initials inside it

blocks.note: a beam is a broad smile
the initials of the Liberal Democrats, a British political party, taken inside the smile

annotation.surface: An old woman smiles on meeting a Liberal Democrat canvasser.
annotation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are a British party, abbreviated LD.
annotation.definitionFit: Beldam is an archaic word for an old woman, often a hag.

entries.clue: Get ace group of singers on the radio (7)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: on the radio, words are heard, not seen spelt

blocks.note: A = ace, as on playing cards

blocks.clueFragment: group of singers on the radio
blocks.note: a choir, said aloud 'kwire', which older English also spelt quire

annotation.surface: Book a first-rate choir for a radio broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound of ACQUIRE is 'a-kwire': A for ace, then CHOIR said aloud, which is also spelt QUIRE in older English.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to come into possession of something.

entries.clue: Madcap Tchaikovsky pens something that shows he’s human (7)

indicatorNotes.pens: the two words pen, that is enclose, the answer

annotation.surface: A crazy Tchaikovsky writes something that proves he is only human.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pens' looks like the composer writing music; it means the words enclose the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A CAPTCHA is a website test that shows the user is a human, not a bot.

entries.clue: Med city canal I’ve restored (8)

indicatorNotes.restored: the letters are rebuilt into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone boasts of having restored a canal in a Mediterranean city.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in I've is ignored, as punctuation always is in wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Valencia is a Spanish city on the Mediterranean coast.

entries.clue: Counterfeit piece leaving in the direction of EU nation (7)

annotation.definitionNote: counterfeit here is the noun: a fake

indicatorNotes.leaving: the piece departs from the nation's name

blocks.note: heading for a place = in its direction
a man is a chess or draughts piece
GERMANY, with the piece leaving it

annotation.surface: A counterfeit coin heads for an EU country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a coin in a counterfeit story; it is a man on a chessboard, taken out of GERMANY.
annotation.definitionFit: A counterfeit is a forgery, a fake made to pass as genuine.

entries.clue: Todd lugs around a product of mine (4,4)

annotation.surface: A man called Todd hauls about something he has made.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mine' pretends to be the possessive, as if Todd were lugging the speaker's product; it is a gold mine.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: fine grains of the metal are one of the things a mine yields.

entries.clue: I start to get excited after report of you getting introduced to Joe Strummer (9)

indicatorNotes.to get excited: letters that get excited jump about into a new order
indicatorNotes.getting introduced to: the U is put inside Joe's letters

blocks.note: the letter U; goes inside GI: G(U)I

annotation.surface: A fan gets excited on being introduced to Joe Strummer, of The Clash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joe Strummer' reads as the punk singer's name; it splits into Joe, the GI, and a strummer, the definition. The anagram comes first in the clue but last in the answer, since it sits 'after' the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A description by action: strumming the strings is what this player does, and Joe Strummer was one.

entries.clue: Starve in the morning? Seafood sandwiches! (6)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the fish holds the morning between its slices

blocks.note: fish is seafood; it sandwiches the morning between its letters

annotation.surface: Someone skipping breakfast is offered seafood sandwiches instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like lunch; it is a verb, the fish enclosing AM.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, somewhat old-fashioned: both verbs mean to go, or leave someone, without food.

entries.clue: Hurry up mum, run both taps – that’s an order! (5,5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the answer rather than replacing it: quick march is a command

blocks.note: the cold and hot taps, marked C and H

annotation.surface: A child is ordered to hurry and fill the bath from both taps.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a parent hurrying someone into the bath. Taps in Britain are labelled C and H, cold and hot.
annotation.definitionFit: Quick march is a military order to march at normal pace.

entries.clue: Organ stop fed by electronic pulse (6,4)

indicatorNotes.fed by: the stop is fed an E, taking it inside

blocks.note: e- as in e-mail; goes inside: B(E)AN

annotation.surface: An organ stop is powered by an electronic pulse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ stop' and 'pulse' both pretend to be musical or electrical; the organ is a kidney and a pulse is an edible seed.
annotation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes, and the kidney bean is one.

entries.clue: Additional matter to absorb student (4)

indicatorNotes.to absorb: the matter soaks the student up inside it

blocks.note: learner, from the L plate a British learner driver displays; taken inside the matter

annotation.surface: A student is given extra reading to absorb.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matter' in the medical sense is pus.
annotation.definitionFit: Plus as an adjective means additional or extra, as in a plus factor.

entries.clue: Where to have a cuppa after exercising Great Dane (3,6)

indicatorNotes.exercising: the dog's letters are put through their paces

annotation.surface: A dog walker stops for tea after exercising the Great Dane.
annotation.walkthrough: A cuppa is a British cup of tea.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café where tea is served.

entries.clue: Defeatist, for example, punching local person (8)

indicatorNotes.punching: the example punches its way into the local

blocks.note: a native is a local; the example punches into it after its first letter

annotation.surface: A defeatist lashes out and punches a local.
annotation.walkthrough: Written as 'Defeatist, for example', the surface makes the definition look like the example; the comma ends the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: both describe expecting the worst.

entries.clue: Upright piano in Laos got damaged (8)

annotation.definitionNote: Upright is the noun: a vertical post

indicatorNotes.in: the piano's letter goes in with the rest
indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: An upright piano was damaged in transit to Laos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upright piano' is a single thing in the surface; split it, and 'Upright' is the definition and 'piano' is just P.
annotation.definitionFit: Each goalpost is one of the uprights of a goal.

entries.clue: Son knocked up tailless fish and shellfish (7)

indicatorNotes.knocked up: in a down entry, knocked up means pushed upward, written from the bottom
indicatorNotes.tailless: the fish loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A son whips up a fish and seafood supper.
annotation.walkthrough: The pollack is a food fish related to cod. 'Knocked up' reads as cooked together quickly; in a down entry it lifts the fish upward.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: this fan-shelled bivalve is one kind of shellfish.

entries.clue: Starts to dredge English river south of tight bend (7)

indicatorNotes.Starts to: take the start of each word
indicatorNotes.south of: in a down entry, the letters go below the other piece

blocks.note: first letters of Dredge English River

annotation.surface: Workers begin dredging an English river below a sharp bend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight bend' is one phrase in the surface; 'tight' is the stingy MEAN and 'bend' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A geographer's term: named after a winding Turkish river, it is a loop-shaped bend in a watercourse.

entries.clue: Lover boy‘s painful back (4)

annotation.surface: A Romeo complains of a painful back.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek boy god of love.

entries.clue: Little ‘un born and bred in Wensleydale? (10)

annotation.definition: Little ‘un born and bred in Wensleydale?

blocks.note: read as a Yorkshire child, and meant as a tiny creature
read as raised in the Yorkshire valley, and meant as breeding inside the crumbly cheese named after it

annotation.surface: A child born and raised in a Yorkshire dale.
annotation.walkthrough: Wensleydale is a Yorkshire valley and also the crumbly cheese made there. The 'little one' is a tiny mite that breeds inside such a cheese, not a Yorkshire child.
annotation.definitionFit: Cheese mites are tiny creatures that live and multiply in cheese.

entries.clue: Diocese observed a bit of back and forth (6)

annotation.definition: a bit of back and forth

blocks.note: a bishop's see is his diocese

annotation.surface: A diocese sees a certain amount of debate going to and fro.
annotation.walkthrough: A see-saw movement is one that goes back and forth, and a seesaw is a spell of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense of the playground plank: any spell of swinging one way then the other.

entries.clue: Annual back in library in good time (6)

indicatorNotes.back in: the letter at the back of the word

annotation.surface: A library's annual is back on the shelves in good time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Annual' could be the noun, a yearbook; it is the adjective, and 'back' is not a reversal but the tail of library.
annotation.definitionFit: Annual and yearly both mean happening once a year.

entries.clue: Football: Ancelotti fields brave attacker (8)

indicatorNotes.fields: the words field, or hold, the answer as a team fields players

annotation.surface: A football report: manager Carlo Ancelotti picks a bold striker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fields' is team selection in a football story; here it means the words hold the answer. 'Attacker' pretends to be a striker, not a knight.
annotation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot was the bravest knight of the Round Table, a formidable attacker in battle.

entries.clue: Test ground eggs first in laboratory (4)

indicatorNotes.first in: the first letter of the word

annotation.surface: Eggs are ground up first in a laboratory test.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like crushed; it is a sports ground. THE OVAL is a London cricket ground where Test matches are played.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this London venue is one of the English grounds that stage Test matches.

entries.clue: Large former prisoner pinches international wordbook (7)

indicatorNotes.pinches: the ex-con grabs the letter and holds it inside

blocks.note: an ex-con; wraps round I: EX(I)CON

annotation.surface: A big ex-convict steals a foreign dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinches' reads as stealing, apt for a former prisoner; it means enclosing.
annotation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, a book of words.

entries.clue: One collapsed beneath the stalls in Covent Garden? (5,3)

annotation.definition: One collapsed beneath the stalls in Covent Garden?

blocks.note: read as a person who fainted, and meant as an object folded flat

blocks.clueFragment: beneath the stalls in Covent Garden?
blocks.note: read as lying under the seats after fainting, and meant as stowed under a seat at the Royal Opera House

annotation.surface: Someone faints under the seating at the Royal Opera House.
annotation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is home to London's Royal Opera House. The 'one collapsed' sounds like a fainting patron; it is a collapsible top hat, folded flat and stowed under the seat in the stalls.
annotation.definitionFit: An opera hat is a collapsible top hat designed to fit under a theatre seat.

entries.clue: Friendly agreement between ten teams holds (7)

indicatorNotes.holds: the phrase holds the answer inside it

blocks.note: seven letters running from the last E of 'between' into 'teams'

annotation.surface: A friendly agreement among ten teams is holding.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Holds' looks like the agreement lasting; it is the hiding instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding, especially between nations.
